newsitem.title: USA: CME lumber futures end up on shortcovering.
newsitem.headline: CME lumber futures end up on shortcovering.

text.p: Trading remained light and CME lumber finished mostly higher on continued support from pre-weekend shortcovering, traders said.
Futures finished mostly $4.00 to $1.00 higher, with September up $2.10 at $347.10 per tbf and November up most at $347.60.
Light shortcovering prompted by the discount of futures to cash was adequate enough to support futures despite a weak undertone to cash, traders said.
Evening up of positions ahead of the weekend made for mixed trade at times, they added.

Random Lengths quoted cash spruce at $355 per tbf, unchanged from midweek and up $3 from last Friday. Some producers openly admitted they would be forced to drop prices by next week if sales didn't pick up, but others claimed order files into September, they said.
